vendors.name: Oracle Aconex
vendors.tagline: Oracle's cloud document control and project collaboration platform
vendors.market_position: Oracle Aconex is a cloud platform where every party on a project shares documents, formal correspondence (Mail) and review workflows in one auditable record; Oracle announced its purchase of Aconex in December 2017. Oracle's Aconex status page lists a Middle East (MEA) instance and a separate Saudi Arabia (KSA1) instance. Construction Week reported in March 2017 that Aconex had signed a five-year deal with Dubai Airports.
pros: Documents, Mail and approval workflows in one shared project record
Middle East (MEA) and Saudi (KSA1) instances listed by Oracle
Oracle Aconex Mobile app for site teams
Still developed: Oracle announced new Aconex capabilities in April 2026
cons: No public prices: quote from Oracle
Built for multi-party projects, more than a small contractor needs
Not an accounting or VAT tool
Support Central help is not offered in Arabic
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public price list found.
vendors.ae_specific_note: Aconex suits main contractors, consultants and clients who need one shared record of documents and correspondence across many companies. It does not keep VAT records or issue tax invoices, so pair it with a VAT-ready accounting system.

vendors.name: Oracle Primavera P6
vendors.tagline: Oracle's critical-path scheduling and project portfolio software
vendors.market_position: Primavera P6 is Oracle's project scheduling line: P6 Enterprise Project Portfolio Management (EPPM), which Oracle offers on-premises or in the cloud, and the desktop P6 Professional. Oracle's documentation describes P6 Professional as designed for large-scale, multifaceted projects, with unlimited resources and target plans. Both products are documented up to version 26.
pros: Critical-path scheduling with unlimited resources and target plans (per Oracle)
Portfolio and multi-project planning in P6 EPPM
P6 EPPM runs on-premises or in Oracle's cloud
Current release (version 26) documented on docs.oracle.com
cons: No public prices: quote from Oracle or a partner
Built for professional planners; a learning curve for occasional users
More than a small firm's job schedule needs
Scheduling only: no accounting or VAT
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public price list found.
vendors.ae_specific_note: If a client contract specifies the programme format or scheduling software, confirm the requirement before you buy. P6 handles scheduling only, so VAT records and invoicing stay in your accounting system.

vendors.name: Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud)
vendors.tagline: Autodesk's construction platform, now sold as Autodesk Forma
vendors.market_position: Autodesk moved Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC) into its Autodesk Forma brand on 24 March 2026 and renamed the products, for example Forma Build, Forma Data Management, Forma Takeoff and Forma Estimate. Autodesk sells them in three quote-based bundles, Model Management, Preconstruction and Construction Operations, which also include Navisworks Manage, BuildingConnected Pro, ProEst and Pype tools.
pros: Model coordination, design collaboration and document management in one account
Bundles run from takeoff, estimating and bidding to field operations and closeout
User-, project- and account-based pricing options (per Autodesk)
30-day money-back guarantee stated on the pricing page
cons: No public prices for the construction bundles: quote-based
Product names changed in March 2026, so older guides use ACC names
Not an accounting or VAT tool
BIM depth is more than simple jobs need
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based: Autodesk's construction pricing page lists three bundles (Model Management, Preconstruction, Construction Operations) with 'Get a quote' and no prices; Autodesk says it offers user-, project- and account-based pricing and a 30-day money-back guarantee.
vendors.ae_specific_note: Global Construction Review reported in November 2023 that from 1 January 2024 Dubai Municipality would accept permit applications only with BIM models for buildings above 20 floors (architectural models) or 40 floors (structural), large complexes, specialised buildings such as hospitals and universities, and all government projects, following the Dubai BIM standard. The mandate names no software, so Autodesk Forma is one option among several BIM tools.

vendors.name: Procore
vendors.tagline: Construction project management, quality, safety and financials
vendors.market_position: Procore Technologies (NYSE: PCOR) opened its first MENA office in Dubai Internet City in September 2022 and runs a UAE site with a Dubai phone line. Its UAE site lists project management, quality and safety, financial management and Procore AI on one platform. Every contract includes unlimited users and data storage, per Procore.
pros: Unlimited users and data storage in every contract (per Procore)
Project management, quality and safety, and financial tools on one platform
500+ integrations, including Xero and Sage 50 Accounts Cloud (per Procore)
Dubai office and a UAE phone line
cons: No public prices: annual fee per product based on turnover
UAE site is English only, with no Arabic option
Not an accounting system: UAE VAT returns stay elsewhere
A full rollout across projects and subcontractors takes planning
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. Procore's UAE pricing page says it charges an upfront annual fee per product based on your annual turnover, with unlimited users and data storage included.
vendors.ae_specific_note: Procore's financial tools cover budgets, forecasts, change orders and payment applications, not UAE VAT accounting, so keep a VAT-ready accounting system alongside it. Procore lists connectors for accounting tools such as Xero and Sage 50 Accounts Cloud.

vendors.name: Bentley Systems
vendors.tagline: Infrastructure design, project delivery and 4D construction software
vendors.market_position: Bentley Systems makes infrastructure engineering software, including ProjectWise for project delivery, SYNCHRO 4D for construction planning, OpenRoads Designer for roads and MicroStation for CAD, and has an office in City Tower 2 on Sheikh Zayed Road, Dubai. It publishes USD prices for 12-month Virtuoso subscriptions on its website, with enterprise licensing by quote. Buyers of its ProjectWise bundle can choose the UAE as their data storage location.
pros: Published online prices for single licences (USD, 12-month subscriptions)
ProjectWise bundle data can be stored in the UAE
4D construction planning in SYNCHRO 4D
Dubai office on Sheikh Zayed Road
cons: High per-seat prices for design tools (OpenRoads Designer from $7,226 a year)
Built for infrastructure and civil work more than building fit-out
Specialist engineering tools with a learning curve
Enterprise terms and bundles beyond the list are by quote
vendors.typical_pricing: Published on bentley.com (USD, 12-month Virtuoso subscription, 1 licence): Bentley Infrastructure Cloud Connect from $312, ProjectWise from $960, SYNCHRO 4D from $4,980 (includes 2 Keys for training or services), OpenRoads Designer from $7,226. ProjectWise Bundle from $10,440 (15 Connect and 6 ProjectWise subscriptions). Enterprise licensing by quote.
vendors.ae_specific_note: Most relevant for infrastructure and civil packages such as roads, utilities and large civil works rather than standard building fit-out. Buyers of the ProjectWise bundle can pick the UAE as their data storage location.

vendors.name: PlanRadar
vendors.tagline: Site inspections, snagging, defects and site documentation
vendors.market_position: PlanRadar, founded in Vienna in 2013, is a site documentation, inspection and defect-management app with a Dubai office in Boulevard Plaza Tower 1, Downtown. PlanRadar says it has more than 200,000 users in 75+ countries, and its Arabic-language UAE page names customers including Shapoorji Pallonji, Amana Steel Buildings and National Central Cooling Company. It publishes per-user prices, and subcontractors join free on every plan.
pros: Published per-user prices and a 30-day free trial with no credit card
Unlimited subcontractors free on every plan
Arabic-language UAE website and pricing page
Dubai office in Downtown
cons: Site execution only, not scheduling or accounting
Starter and Pro are capped at 10 users; more needs Enterprise
4% innovation fee on the annual fee from the second billing period
Prices shown in USD, EUR, GBP or AUD, not AED
vendors.typical_pricing: Published (USD, per user per month, excluding VAT): Basic $32 (1 user, 10 plans), Starter $107 (up to 10 users, 30 plans per user), Pro $159 (up to 10 users, 100 plans per user, 1 BIM model per user); Enterprise by quote. Monthly or annual billing, with annual saving more than 10%; PlanRadar bills annually in advance unless the contract says otherwise and adds a 4% innovation fee from the second billing period. 30-day free trial.
vendors.ae_specific_note: PlanRadar runs an Arabic-language UAE site and a Dubai office. It suits contractors who want digital snagging, inspections and handover records without an enterprise rollout; VAT invoicing stays in your accounting system.

vendors.name: First Bit ERP
vendors.tagline: Construction ERP for UAE contractors: costing, procurement, accounting and payroll
vendors.market_position: First Bit sells a construction ERP that it says is built exclusively for UAE contractors, covering project cost control, procurement, accounting, VAT and corporate tax, HR and payroll, equipment and warehouse. The company was founded in Moscow in 1997, says it has been in the UAE for 13 years with a separate UAE legal entity since 2022, and has an office in Falcon House, Dubai Investment Park. First Bit says more than 2,000 UAE companies have chosen it.
pros: Built for contracting: project cost control, procurement and equipment
VAT returns and corporate tax calculation built in (per First Bit)
Arabic-English bilingual reporting (per First Bit)
Cloud or on-premises, with implementation, training and support in the subscription
cons: No public prices: quote based on users, deployment and scope
Phased ERP implementation takes time
More system than a small trade firm needs
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. First Bit says the price depends on company size, number of users, cloud or on-premises deployment and implementation scope, and that the subscription includes implementation, training, maintenance and support.
vendors.ae_specific_note: First Bit describes the software as FTA-approved for VAT and says it covers corporate tax and supports UAE e-invoicing integration as the rules roll out. The FTA publishes a list of accredited tax accounting software with a validity date for each product, so check First Bit's current entry there before relying on the approval. First Bit is not on the Ministry of Finance list of accredited e-invoicing service providers (checked 30 September 2026), so UAE e-invoices would go through a separate accredited provider.

vendors.name: Focus Softnet
vendors.tagline: ERP suite with project costing, contract management and CAFM
vendors.market_position: Focus Softnet, established in 1992, sells the Focus X cloud ERP and related products including CRM, HCM, warehouse, POS and Focus CAFM, and says it operates from 27 offices in 17 countries. Its UAE site lists a head office in Dubai Internet City plus offices in Abu Dhabi and Sharjah. Focus Softnet is on the Ministry of Finance list of accredited e-invoicing service providers (accreditation number 134577).
pros: Ministry of Finance accredited e-invoicing service provider
Project costing, contract management and equipment servicing modules
Focus CAFM for facility work orders and maintenance
Offices in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah
cons: No public prices: demo and quote only
A general ERP with construction modules, not a construction-only product
Broad suite, more than small firms need
ERP implementation effort
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. Focus's UAE pages offer a free demo and a call-back instead.
vendors.ae_specific_note: Focus Softnet appears on the UAE Ministry of Finance list of accredited e-invoicing service providers (number 134577, list updated 30 September 2026), and says its e-invoicing product is OpenPeppol certified for the PINT-AE format. Compare its project costing depth with construction-specific ERPs before choosing.

vendors.name: PACT ERP
vendors.tagline: Modular ERP with contracting, procurement and WPS payroll
vendors.market_position: PACT Software, which says it has provided ERP since 1998, sells a modular ERP covering finance, procurement, inventory, projects and HR and payroll, with a construction and contracting solution, and has an office in SIT Tower, Dubai Silicon Oasis. PACT Software Services LLC is on the Ministry of Finance list of accredited e-invoicing service providers (accreditation number 129353). PACT says it has more than 12,000 customers worldwide.
pros: Ministry of Finance accredited e-invoicing service provider
Project planning, budgeting and cost control for contractors
Payroll with WPS salary file generation (per PACT)
Office in Dubai Silicon Oasis
cons: No public prices: quote only
Construction page does not detail BOQ, retention or progress billing
ERP setup effort
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices.
vendors.ae_specific_note: PACT Software Services LLC appears on the UAE Ministry of Finance list of accredited e-invoicing service providers (number 129353, list updated 30 September 2026), and PACT says its payroll module generates WPS salary files. Ask for a demo of BOQ, retention and progress billing, which its construction page does not detail.

vendors.name: Sage (200 / 300)
vendors.tagline: Sage mid-market finance and ERP (Sage 300, X3, Intacct) sold through UAE partners
vendors.market_position: Sage sells its mid-market finance and ERP products in the UAE through business partners. It launched Sage Intacct, its cloud financial management platform, in the UAE on 23 October 2025, to be delivered through certified business partners. Sage partner SynergERP, which has a Dubai office, sells Sage X3, Sage Intacct and Sage 300 in the UAE.
pros: Choice of Sage 300, Sage X3 or Sage Intacct through UAE partners
Multi-entity and multi-currency cloud finance in Sage Intacct
UAE VAT module for Sage Intacct (Intaxx) built by a Sage partner
cons: Sold through partners: quote only, no public UAE prices
Construction features depend on the partner's set-up
UAE VAT on Sage Intacct needs a partner-built module
Not a site, scheduling or BIM tool
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based through Sage business partners; no public UAE prices found.
vendors.ae_specific_note: Sage is not on the UAE Ministry of Finance list of accredited e-invoicing service providers (checked 30 September 2026), so e-invoices would go through a separate accredited provider. For Sage Intacct, UAE VAT returns, FTA audit files and tax invoices come from the Intaxx module, which partner SynergERP says Sage contracted it to build. It suits firms where finance and cost control come first and a partner configures it for contracting.

vendors.name: Zoho (Projects / Books / FSM)
vendors.tagline: Zoho Books accounting with Projects and FSM for small firms
vendors.market_position: Zoho offers separate apps that small contractors can combine: Zoho Books for accounting and UAE VAT, Zoho Projects for project management and Zoho FSM for field-service work orders and dispatch. Zoho Books has a UAE edition with AED prices and an Arabic option, and Zoho says it files VAT returns directly with EmaraTax. Zoho Software Trading LLC is on the Ministry of Finance list of accredited e-invoicing service providers (accreditation number 121988).
pros: Published AED prices for Zoho Books, with a free plan
Ministry of Finance accredited e-invoicing service provider
VAT return filing to EmaraTax and corporate tax reports (per Zoho)
Free plans in Books, Projects (up to 5 users) and FSM (30 appointments a month)
cons: Not built for construction: general accounting, project and field-service apps
You assemble and pay for several apps
Zoho Books plans cap users and invoices per year
vendors.typical_pricing: Zoho Books UAE (AED per organisation per month, excluding local taxes): Free (1 user plus an accountant, revenue up to AED 200,000 a year), Standard AED 60 billed yearly or AED 69 monthly (3 users), Professional AED 90 or AED 129 (5 users), Premium AED 120 or AED 159 (10 users), Elite AED 280 or AED 349 (10 users), Ultimate AED 660 or AED 799 (15 users); extra users AED 8 a month billed yearly or AED 10 monthly. Zoho Projects (free for up to 5 users) and Zoho FSM (free for 30 appointments a month) are priced separately.
vendors.ae_specific_note: Zoho Software Trading LLC is on the UAE Ministry of Finance list of accredited e-invoicing service providers (number 121988, list updated 30 September 2026), and Zoho Books can send e-invoices in the PINT-AE format through Peppol. With VAT and corporate tax records in Zoho Books, small contractors get a low-cost accounting base and can add Projects or FSM as they grow.

vendors.name: Horizon FMS (FIT)
vendors.tagline: Dubai-built CAFM: assets, planned maintenance and work orders
vendors.market_position: Horizon FMS is a web-based computer-aided facility management (CAFM) system with mobile access from Frontline Information Technology LLC (FIT), a Dubai software company that says it has operated since 1992 and has an office in Al Karama. It covers assets, preventive maintenance, work orders and contracts for hard services such as HVAC, electrical and plumbing and soft services such as cleaning and security. FIT also sells the Horizon EBS ERP, Horizon HRMS and Horizon eProcure.
pros: Dubai vendor with an office in Al Karama
Assets, preventive maintenance, work orders and contracts in one system
Covers hard and soft FM services, with mobile access
Same vendor sells Horizon EBS ERP, HRMS and eProcure
cons: No public prices: quote only
FM-focused, not construction project management
VAT features are documented for Horizon EBS, not Horizon FMS
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices.
vendors.ae_specific_note: A locally built option for UAE facilities-management and MEP-maintenance firms that want CAFM from a Dubai vendor. FIT's VAT claims (FTA-format tax invoices in English and Arabic, VAT 201 returns) are made for its Horizon EBS ERP, and FIT is not on the Ministry of Finance list of accredited e-invoicing service providers (checked 30 September 2026).

vendors.name: FSM Grid
vendors.tagline: Field-service management platform from FSM Global, a Ducont Systems company with a Dubai office
vendors.market_position: FSM Grid is a field-service management platform from FSM Global Technologies, which says it is a subsidiary of Ducont Systems, an IT products and services provider based in the Middle East. It covers scheduling and dispatch, work orders, parts and inventory, quotations, contracts and SLAs, a customer portal, IoT integration and AI-driven predictive maintenance. FSM Global lists an office in Dubai Outsource City and says more than 75,000 field-service users rely on its software.
pros: Scheduling, dispatch, work orders and parts inventory in one platform
IoT integration and AI-driven predictive maintenance modules
Dubai office and English/Arabic support in the Middle East, per FSM Global
Dedicated HVAC industry module and contracts/SLA tracking
cons: No public prices; demo and quote only
Not an accounting system: invoicing relies on integration with accounting software
UAE VAT handling is not described on the vendor's site
Industry focus is telecom, manufacturing, medical equipment and HVAC rather than general building trades
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices (demo on request).
vendors.ae_specific_note: FSM Global lists a Dubai office in Dubai Outsource City and says FSM Grid supports English and Arabic in the Middle East. Its site does not describe UAE VAT or FTA e-invoicing features, so confirm tax handling with the vendor or keep invoicing in your accounting system.

vendors.name: Dubai Municipality (Contractor Licensing)
vendors.tagline: Dubai's regulator for contractor registration, classification and building permits
vendors.market_position: Dubai Municipality licenses contracting companies and engineering consultancies in Dubai and runs building permit procedures. Dubai Law No. 7 of 2025, published on 15 July 2025 and in force six months later, makes entry in an electronic Contractors Register kept by the Municipality mandatory, with classification handled through an emirate-wide system linked to the Invest in Dubai platform. The law covers contractors across the emirate, including free zones and DIFC, but excludes airport infrastructure work.
pros: One emirate-wide Contractors Register kept by Dubai Municipality
Registration and classification through a system linked to the Invest in Dubai platform
Classification by activity and category, based on experience and financial and technical capability
Professional competency certificates for contractors' technical staff
cons: Existing contractors must comply within one year of the law taking effect (extendable by the committee)
Fines of AED 1,000 to AED 100,000, doubled up to AED 200,000 for a repeat within a year
Violations can also bring suspension, downgrading or removal from the Register
Fees are not listed on Dubai Municipality's public pages
vendors.typical_pricing: Government fees per service; the Dubai Municipality pages read on 2026-09-30 do not list contractor registration, classification or permit fees, so check the service card on the Dubai Municipality services hub.
vendors.ae_specific_note: Under Dubai Law No. 7 of 2025, no one may carry on or advertise contracting work in Dubai without a trade licence and entry in the Contractors Register, and clients may not hire unregistered firms. Contractors already working when the law took effect have one year from that date to comply, which the committee can extend by a further year.

vendors.name: Ministry of Energy & Infrastructure (MOEI)
vendors.tagline: Federal registration and e-qualification of contractors for MOEI engineering projects
vendors.market_position: The Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure (MOEI) registers and e-qualifies consultants, contractors and suppliers to carry out its engineering projects. It also runs a separate, no-fee contractor registration for its housing assistance programme, so contractors can work for programme beneficiaries. MOEI qualification sits alongside emirate-level rules such as Dubai Municipality's Contractors Register, not in place of them.
pros: Qualifies consultants, contractors and suppliers for MOEI engineering projects
New registration AED 500 with no annual renewal fee, per MOEI's service listing
Separate no-fee registration to work on housing assistance programme projects
cons: Only relevant if you bid for MOEI projects or housing assistance work
Does not replace emirate-level trade licensing or registration
MOEI's fee list includes an AED 500 annual fine (AED 100 for soil test consultants)
vendors.typical_pricing: E-qualification for MOEI engineering projects, per MOEI's service listing: new registration AED 500; annual renewal nil; certificate modification AED 250; annual fine AED 500 (AED 100 for soil test consultants). Contractor registration for the housing assistance programme: no fee.
vendors.ae_specific_note: Federal and emirate-level registration are separate: MOEI e-qualification covers MOEI's own engineering projects, while contracting anywhere in Dubai also needs a trade licence and entry in Dubai Municipality's Contractors Register under Dubai Law No. 7 of 2025. Check the rules of each emirate you work in.

vendors.name: UAE VAT (Federal Tax Authority)
vendors.tagline: UAE VAT at 5%, administered by the Federal Tax Authority since 1 January 2018
vendors.market_position: The Federal Tax Authority (FTA) administers UAE VAT, introduced on 1 January 2018 at 5%. A business must register once its taxable supplies and imports exceed AED 375,000 over 12 months, and may register voluntarily from AED 187,500. Registration, returns and payments run through the FTA's EmaraTax platform, accessed with UAE Pass, and each return and payment is due within 28 days of the end of the tax period.
pros: One federal VAT regime at 5%
Free registration through EmaraTax (the FTA quotes 20 business days to process)
Published thresholds: AED 375,000 mandatory, AED 187,500 voluntary
FTA refund scheme for UAE nationals building a new home
cons: Invoicing software must produce UAE VAT invoices and returns at 5%
Return and payment due within 28 days of each tax period end
FTA services are available only online through UAE Pass and EmaraTax
vendors.typical_pricing: VAT registration is free (FTA service card); VAT is charged at 5%.
vendors.ae_specific_note: Set your invoicing and accounting software up for UAE VAT at 5% and FTA returns filed through EmaraTax. If you build homes for UAE nationals, keep proper tax invoices: the owner can claim VAT on the new residence back from the FTA within 12 months of completion.

vendors.name: UAE E-Invoicing (Peppol)
vendors.tagline: UAE e-invoicing through accredited Peppol service providers, mandatory in phases from January 2027
vendors.market_position: The Ministry of Finance runs UAE e-invoicing on a decentralised five-corner model based on the OpenPeppol standard: each business appoints an Accredited Service Provider (ASP) that exchanges invoices with the buyer's provider and reports the data to the Federal Tax Authority. It covers business-to-business and business-to-government invoices; business-to-consumer transactions stay outside the system until the Minister decides otherwise. A pilot and voluntary adoption began on 1 July 2026, businesses with revenue of AED 50 million or more must go live by 1 January 2027, and smaller businesses by 1 July 2027.
pros: Published phased timeline set by Ministerial decision
Public Ministry of Finance list of ASPs (60 accredited and 3 pre-approved on 30 September 2026)
Business-to-consumer invoices are outside the system for now
Businesses under AED 50 million revenue have until 1 July 2027
cons: Revenue of AED 50 million or more: appoint an ASP by 30 October 2026 and go live by 1 January 2027
Below AED 50 million: appoint an ASP by 31 March 2027 and go live by 1 July 2027
You need a contract with an Accredited Service Provider, not just e-invoice-capable software
Violations and penalties are set by Cabinet Decision No. 106 of 2025
vendors.typical_pricing: No fee for businesses appears on the Ministry of Finance pages; you pay your chosen Accredited Service Provider, which sets its own prices.
vendors.ae_specific_note: If your revenue is AED 50 million or more, the deadline to appoint an Accredited Service Provider is 30 October 2026 (moved from 31 July 2026 by Ministerial Decision No. 66 of 2026), with go-live on 1 January 2027. Smaller contractors must appoint one by 31 March 2027 and go live by 1 July 2027, so check that your accounting software works with a provider on the Ministry of Finance list.

vendors.name: MOHRE & Emiratisation (Nafis)
vendors.tagline: Federal labour ministry that sets and enforces private-sector Emiratisation targets
vendors.market_position: The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE) sets Emiratisation targets for private companies and collects financial contributions from those that miss them. MOHRE requires companies with 50 or more employees to raise their Emirati share by 2% a year, with a first-half deadline of 30 June, and says targeted companies should reach 10% by the end of 2026. Companies with 20-49 employees in 14 sectors had to hire one Emirati in 2024 and another in 2025, and MOHRE points employers to the Nafis platform for help finding Emirati candidates.
pros: Published targets with half-yearly deadlines (30 June for the first half of 2026)
Nafis platform helps employers find qualified Emirati candidates
Contribution amounts announced before collection (2025 amounts collected in January 2026)
cons: From 1 July 2026, AED 10,000 a month (AED 120,000 a year) per unfilled position for companies with 50 or more employees
Companies with 20-49 employees in 14 sectors paid AED 108,000 per Emirati not hired under 2025 targets
Fines of up to AED 500,000 for circumventing targets, per MOHRE
Minimum wage for Emiratis in the private sector raised to AED 6,000 a month
vendors.typical_pricing: Government service fees apply per MOHRE service; missed Emiratisation targets carry financial contributions (AED 120,000 a year per unfilled position from 1 July 2026 for companies with 50 or more employees).
vendors.ae_specific_note: If you have 50 or more employees, or 20-49 employees in one of the 14 targeted sectors, track your Emirati headcount against MOHRE's half-yearly targets: each missed position costs a financial contribution. Your payroll setup should also reflect the AED 6,000 monthly minimum wage for Emiratis in the private sector.

vendors.name: Abu Dhabi DMT & Estidama
vendors.tagline: Abu Dhabi building permits, contractor classification and the Estidama Pearl rating
vendors.market_position: The Department of Municipalities and Transport (DMT) handles building permits in Abu Dhabi, requested through TAMM and its electronic building permit system, and classifies engineering contractors and consulting offices in grades from Special to Sixth. DMT also governs the Estidama Pearl Rating System, which rates projects from one to five Pearls. Privately funded projects need at least one Pearl and government-funded projects at least two to obtain a building permit.
pros: Published Estidama minimums: one Pearl for private projects, two for government-funded ones
Contractor and consultant classification in grades from Special to Sixth
Building permits requested online through TAMM
Pearl Qualified Professionals trained to guide projects through Estidama
cons: An Estidama Pearl rating is a condition of the building permit
Separate regime from Dubai Municipality's registration and permits
Estidama includes mandatory credits, which adds design and documentation work
Fees are not listed on DMT's public pages
vendors.typical_pricing: Government fees per service; the DMT pages read on 2026-09-30 do not list permit, classification or Estidama fees, so check the service on TAMM.
vendors.ae_specific_note: Abu Dhabi and Dubai run separate systems: Abu Dhabi projects go through DMT classification, permits and Estidama Pearl ratings, while Dubai work needs entry in Dubai Municipality's Contractors Register under Dubai Law No. 7 of 2025. If you work in both emirates, expect separate registrations and different compliance paperwork.

vendors.name: Dubai BIM Mandate
vendors.tagline: Dubai Municipality's BIM model requirement for large and specialised building applications
vendors.market_position: Dubai Municipality announced in an October 2023 circular that from 1 January 2024 it would accept planning applications for a wide range of buildings only with a BIM model, as reported by Global Construction Review. Architectural models are required for buildings over 20 floors or complexes over 20,000 sq m, structural models for buildings over 40 floors or complexes over 30,000 sq m, and models are also needed for hospitals, universities and all government projects. Models must follow the Dubai Building Code and the Dubai BIM standard, published on the Dubai Building Standard platform.
pros: Published size thresholds for when a model is required
Projects below the thresholds, other than hospitals, universities and government work, are not covered
One Dubai BIM standard used alongside the Dubai Building Code
cons: Requires BIM-capable design software and staff
Adds modelling work before the planning application
Covers all government projects regardless of size
vendors.typical_pricing: No separate BIM fee found; the model is submitted as part of the planning application.
vendors.ae_specific_note: If you design buildings in Dubai above these thresholds, or for hospitals, universities or government clients, the planning application needs a BIM model to the Dubai BIM standard. Check the current circular on the Dubai Building Standard platform before bidding, as this entry relies on the 2023 announcement.

vendors.name: Sukoon Insurance
vendors.tagline: Dubai insurer, formerly Oman Insurance Company, with ten engineering insurance products
vendors.market_position: Sukoon Insurance, known as Oman Insurance Company until its October 2022 rebrand, began operating in 1975 and is regulated by the Central Bank of the UAE. Its engineering line lists ten products, including Contractor's All Risk, Erection All Risk, Contractor's Plant and Machinery, Machinery Breakdown, Electronic Equipment and Principal's Advance Loss of Profits. Premiums are quoted per risk rather than published.
pros: Ten engineering products, from CAR and EAR to plant, machinery and electronic equipment
Owner-side cover too, with Principal's Advance Loss of Profits for a delayed start
Regulated by the Central Bank of the UAE; operating since 1975
Quotes by phone, email, callback form or branch visit
cons: No public premiums; every policy is quoted
Older contracts and tender documents may still name Oman Insurance Company
Product pages give short summaries, so ask for the full policy wording
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public premiums. Sukoon takes quote requests by phone (800 785666), email or callback form.
vendors.ae_specific_note: Sukoon's engineering line covers contractor-side risks (CAR, EAR, plant and machinery) and the project owner's Advance Loss of Profits with one insurer. Documents from before October 2022 may refer to it as Oman Insurance Company.

vendors.name: ADNIC (Abu Dhabi National Insurance Company)
vendors.tagline: Abu Dhabi insurer founded in 1972, with construction, engineering and liability cover for contractors
vendors.market_position: Abu Dhabi National Insurance Company (ADNIC) was founded in 1972, is listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange and is licensed by the Central Bank of the UAE. Its construction and engineering line covers Contractors All-Risk, Erection All-Risk, Contractor's Plant and Machinery, Machinery Breakdown, Electronic Equipment and Advance Loss of Profits, and its liability line adds workmen's compensation, public liability, professional indemnity and decennial liability.
pros: Project cover (CAR, EAR, plant and machinery) and statutory liability cover from one insurer
Workmen's compensation, professional indemnity and decennial liability on its liability page
Downloadable proposal forms plus phone, email and callback channels
cons: No public premiums; every policy is quoted
Comparing it with other insurers means collecting several quotes
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public premiums. ADNIC takes requests by phone (8008040), email, callback form or downloadable proposal forms.
vendors.ae_specific_note: Useful when you want CAR, workmen's compensation, professional indemnity and decennial liability from the same company. If a project owner requires a rated insurer, ask ADNIC for its current rating letter.

vendors.name: Salama (Islamic Arab Insurance)
vendors.tagline: Dubai-listed takaful insurer with engineering, employee compensation and liability cover
vendors.market_position: Salama Islamic Arab Insurance Company is a Shariah-compliant (takaful) insurer based in Dubai, listed on the Dubai Financial Market and regulated by the Central Bank of the UAE; it says it has operated for more than 45 years and protects 450,000 customers. Its engineering and construction line covers Contractor's All Risks, Erection All Risks, Contractor's Plant and Machinery, Machinery Breakdown and Electronic Equipment, and its property and casualty line adds employee compensation, employee liability and public liability.
pros: Shariah-compliant takaful cover for contractors who need it
Engineering set (CAR, EAR, plant, machinery breakdown, electronic equipment) plus employee compensation and public liability
Listed on the Dubai Financial Market and regulated by the Central Bank of the UAE
Quotes by phone (800-725262) or email
cons: No public premiums; every policy is quoted
Shareholders approved a capital restructuring in October 2025
Product pages list covers only, so ask for full policy wordings
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public premiums. Salama takes quote requests by phone (800-725262) or email.
vendors.ae_specific_note: Relevant when a contractor or client requires Shariah-compliant (takaful) cover instead of conventional insurance; Salama offers both the engineering covers and employee compensation and public liability.

vendors.name: ProTenders
vendors.tagline: GCC construction project intelligence and eTendering platform, with free company profiles
vendors.market_position: ProTenders, run by NuServ Ltd and founded in 2011, is a construction intelligence and eTendering platform for developers, consultants, contractors and suppliers across the GCC, including the UAE. Its paid Construction Intelligence product tracks projects with participant details, contacts and notifications, and its eTendering product manages tenders and bids. A free Company Profile lists a firm's projects and products and lets it bid on private tenders; ProTenders lists offices in Abu Dhabi and Montreal.
pros: Built for construction: tracks GCC projects with participating firms and contacts
Free Company Profile with project listing, product catalogue and private tender bidding
eTendering module for issuing and managing tenders
Abu Dhabi office
cons: Construction Intelligence and eTendering are custom-priced; demo required
The free profile gives visibility only; project tracking and contacts are in the paid product
Aimed at developers, consultants, contractors and suppliers rather than homeowners
vendors.typical_pricing: Company Profiles: free. Construction Intelligence and Construction eTendering: custom pricing, no public prices (demo on request).
vendors.ae_specific_note: ProTenders covers UAE projects within its GCC project data and lists an office in Abu Dhabi. It suits firms that sell to developers, consultants and main contractors and want to track GCC projects or respond to private tenders.
